patterns_noted: First cycle lessons: (1) On sharp down days with VIX regime changes, deploy only 15-25% of capital — the cost of being wrong is too high with no journal history. (2) Single-session defensive spikes (XLP +1.71% on crash day) are mean-reverting and should not be bought into; wait for confirmation across multiple timeframes. (3) Rate hike repricing events require distinguishing between NIM beneficiaries (banks/XLF) and rate-sensitive bond proxies (XLU, XLRE) — they often move together initially but diverge fundamentally. (4) Chip sector crashes of $1.3T magnitude (Reuters) historically have follow-through selling; avoid catching falling knives in XLK or semiconductors even if RSI looks oversold. (5) Benchmarking anxiety (seeing rule-based portfolios outperform) should NOT induce premature deployment — cash preservation in a VIX spike is often the alpha move.
